research_question: When does a costly interstate war reduce the subsequent hazard of recurrent crisis rather than perpetuate rivalry?
proposed_mechanism: Repeated crises and mutual mobilization may reinforce antagonism, while sufficiently concentrated war costs may temporarily or durably weaken domestic support for renewed fighting. Distinguish this mechanism from conflict settlement and power-transition commitment problems; do not presume the two studies are contradictory.
search_queries: recurrent crises alliances arms race war escalation
war costs domestic support postwar rivalry
theoretical_question: In a repeated dyadic bargaining model with endogenous domestic support and accumulating hostility, under what conditions does an acute costly war lower the probability of another crisis rather than merely delay it?
candidate_hypotheses: Conditional on pre-war rivalry intensity and territorial issues, greater within-period concentration of realized conflict costs predicts a lower subsequent rate of renewed disputes than similarly costly but dispersed fighting.
The association weakens when unresolved territorial or shifting-power commitment problems remain salient.
After high-cost conflicts, the predicted effect may decay as domestic conflict-support recovers; separate short-run and long-run hazards.
observational_design: Construct a rival-dyad spell/event-time panel. Outcome: time from a conflict to the next interstate militarized dispute or crisis, with right censoring. Include pre-conflict rivalry history, territorial disputes, alliance configuration, prior crises, and conflict duration/severity; explicitly avoid using a retrospectively defined 10-15-year rivalry termination variable as a contemporaneous forecast label.
predictive_design: Compare a pre-registered baseline recurrence hazard with baseline plus concentration / war-cost and conditional mechanisms using chronological out-of-sample splits, Brier score, calibration, and subgroup performance.
identification_risks: War severity and settlement are endogenous; a predictive association is not causal identification.
Rivalry definitions with dispute-free windows cause retrospective label leakage if used as forecasting outcomes.
Historical datasets may have sparse coverage for political support, casualty intensity, and dyadic issue resolution.
